title: Beginner Fundamentals
description: Home row, posture, and the habits that build a calm foundation.

questions.question: Which keys does your left index finger rest on in the home row?
questions.explanation: The left index finger rests on F; the right index finger rests on J. The small bumps help you find them without looking.

questions.question: Where should your wrists sit while typing?
options: Floating, relaxed and level with the keyboard
questions.explanation: Keep wrists floating and relaxed so your fingers can move freely without strain.

questions.question: What is the best way to build typing accuracy first?
questions.explanation: Accuracy comes first; speed is a byproduct of clean, repeated motion.

questions.question: Where should your eyes be while typing?
questions.explanation: Looking at the screen builds touch-typing muscle memory instead of relying on sight.

questions.question: What does WPM measure?
questions.explanation: WPM stands for words per minute — how much clean text you type in sixty seconds.

title: Technique & Rhythm
description: Pacing, rhythm, and the mental side of a steady typing session.

questions.question: What should you do when you make a mistake mid-sentence?
options: Stop and restart the whole session
questions.explanation: A clean recovery keeps rhythm intact. Correct the error and continue without panic.

questions.question: Which approach builds the most durable speed?
questions.explanation: Small, consistent repetitions build muscle memory far better than rare marathon sessions.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a typing rhythm?
questions.explanation: A steady rhythm smooths out hesitation and reduces errors across a session.

questions.question: What does accuracy percentage tell you?
questions.explanation: Accuracy is the share of correct keystrokes out of everything you typed in a session.

questions.question: When should you increase your target speed?
questions.explanation: Raise speed only when you can hold strong accuracy — speed never outruns control.

title: Symbols, Numbers & Pro Form
description: Punctuation, numbers, and the details that separate pros from amateurs.

questions.question: Which finger types the comma and less-than key?
questions.explanation: The right middle finger reaches the comma and less-than keys from the home row.

questions.question: How should you type a capital letter?
options: Hold shift with the opposite hand
Press caps lock for every letter
questions.explanation: Use the shift key on the opposite hand so the typing hand never leaves its anchor.

questions.question: What is the fastest way to type long number sequences?
options: Practice them deliberately until they feel familiar
Look down at the number row
questions.explanation: Deliberate, repeated practice makes numbers and symbols as automatic as letters.

questions.question: Why do professionals practice code-like syntax?
options: Real work is full of symbols, paths, and brackets
questions.explanation: Brackets, slashes, and punctuation appear constantly in technical work — practice the language you actually type.

questions.question: What separates an advanced typist from a beginner?
options: Clean recovery from errors at speed
Using all ten fingers at once
questions.explanation: Advanced typists keep accuracy and composure even when speed and difficulty rise.

title: Speed & Efficiency
description: Measure your understanding of pacing, breaks, and efficient workflows.

questions.question: What matters more than your raw WPM for daily work?
options: A high score in one session
questions.explanation: Reliable, consistent output beats a single impressive burst for real-world work.

questions.question: What should a warm-up session include?
questions.explanation: A short warm-up eases your hands into rhythm and reduces errors in the work that follows.

questions.question: How does error rate affect effective typing speed?
options: Fixing mistakes always slows you down
questions.explanation: Every corrected error costs time — low error rate is what makes raw speed useful.

questions.question: What is the best habit before a long typing block?
options: Setting up a clean, focused workspace
questions.explanation: A calm, prepared environment keeps attention and posture steady for the whole session.

questions.question: How often should you take a break during extended typing?
questions.explanation: Short, regular breaks protect your hands, eyes, and focus so the whole day stays sharp.
